Did anybody command you during the action during the broader area of Pristina or some other entity.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, we were there. We were doing that alone. As I described, I commanded my own men and we followed the plan made by Gergar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And when the action was over did you write a report to some sort of Joint Command or something?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No. This communication was impossible. There was no possibility to send a courier something. We just filed a report with our administration later.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In that action or any other action in which you were involved, did you notice the presence of some Joint Command or any group of civilians who would be involved in any way, at least be merely present in the area of your command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I noticed no such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Matter, Your Honour, at page 46, lines 14 through 15, it says that we just filed a report with our administration later. The witness in Serbian said "uprava policije," which I think is significant. It clarifies to whom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That should be the police, the -- let's have the -- let's have the witness explain who the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'll deal with that, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You were asked when the action was over, did you write a report to the Joint Command or something, and you said, "We just filed a report." Now, where did you file it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not to the Joint Command. When all activities were completed, I filed a report to the police administration in the MUP Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before you let me proceed with the cross-examination, I did not object to the question of Mr. Ivetic, one of them, until I was able to check the transcript, and I think on pages of the transcript 18248 to 250 it was misstated to the witness that nothing had been done with the refugees on -- on behalf of General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's and matter to be dealt with now by you if you wish, Mr. Bakrac, by putting an appropriate question to the witness to clarify the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic my name is Mihajlo Bakrac attorney-at-law appearing here for General Lazarevic. I would like to ask you a few questions. We'll start from the beginning of your statement where in paragraph 4 you say that PJM units were established. As far as I understand, those are specialised units of the police, and they were set up in 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Apart from the name, which was later changed to PJP, did anything change in the substance of this document that established them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: The name was changed to police. Those were regular police forces for regular work and assignments with some additional advanced training for some other kind of work for public gatherings, possibly anti-terrorist activities, for apprehending dangerous criminals, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So one of their tasks was to combat terrorism.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: That's the way it turned out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could we now look at P1508. That's the document creating the PJM. You have already told us that one of their tasks was to fight terrorism, but could we now look at page 3, please. Page 3, "Control and command over the PJM." Could you kindly read the first paragraph, item (c), control and command.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: "Assembly and engagement of the PJM may be ordered only by the minister of the interior or an official authorised by the minister. Specialised units of the militia shall be commanded by the PJM commander with the mediation of detachment commanders and superior officers of lower establishment units. The PJM commander is answerable for his work, mobility, qualification, and work of the PJM to the minister or the person authorised by the minister, whereas other leaders are answerable directly to the superior officer at the PJM."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did this document continue to be in force when PJM became PJP in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't read this very carefully in detail, but in principle this is the way it was created, and I don't think it changed beyond certain limits, but later that actual state of affairs was considerably changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if this is a provision of this document or is it a bylaw on their creation. In 1993, it was formulated that way, and I suppose it didn't change.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Wait a minute. We are not going to make any assumptions. You were the commander of the PJP. 122nd Detachment of the PJP was one of the largest.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: It existed before 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm asking you as the commander of the largest PJP detachment whether command and control really operated that way.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, not really like that. Until the situation occurred in Kosovo it did, but not later. Those were different conditions of work when we had public gatherings and --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What changed in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: The method of work. There were many new reorganisations of detachments in numerical terms, in the names. It used to be 21 and then it became 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Those are formal changes. I'm asking you about control and command. What changed? Who commanded over the PJP in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Until 1997 the commander was Obrad Stevanovic. As far as I remember he became deputy minister -- sorry, assistant minister, and I saw him as the commander but I don't know whether he continued to be commander after that, because the position of assistant minister is several steps higher than PJP commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, Mr. Zivaljevic, are you telling us you don't know who the commander of the PJP was in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw Obrad Stevanovic as the commander, but he was assistant minister, and he came now and then to visit us, but I didn't file reports to him, and I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've thrown doubt into the situation by saying, "I don't know whether he continued to be commander after that." Now, are you actually telling us you cannot say who the commander of the PJP was in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know until 1997 who was the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the answer is -- the answer is you cannot tell us who the commander was in 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that Obrad Stevanovic was still the commander. Whenever I saw him I reported to him what was going on on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why are you expressing doubt? Because obviously this is the sort of thing that makes our life very, very difficult when from a common sense point of view you think a command in your position would know precisely who his leader was, and you come in here and you tell us you're doubtful about it. Now, why are you doubtful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will tell you. When I was sent to carry out tasks in Kosovo and Metohija, I was given a dispatch where it said that Dragan Zivaljevic is being sent to perform the following tasks, and so on. That was stated in the dispatch. I suppose that the minister of the interior made sure that that dispatch was issued, and I think that Rodja Djordjevic as chief of the sector signed the dispatch. I don't have the dispatch in front of me so I can't give you details. So I came to Kosovo and Metohija to perform the tasks pursuant to the task issued to me by the chief the sector. So the minister approved it and chief of sector signed the dispatch. So I suppose that this is the question that should be put to the chief of the sector, not to me. It's not that I don't wish to answer, but now I find myself in this situation that I'm unable to give you a fully accurate, specific answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, ought we to conclude that the system was designed to make sure that even senior officers within the PJP didn't know who the leader was? Was it designed to be confusing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps that's how it appears. The minister is at the top of the pyramid. He's number one. Then the chief of sector is in charge of the police affairs, and then Obrad Stevanovic was assistant minister and in charge of the police -- uniformed police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the first echelon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, I'm now confused. In your statement, in paragraph 7, you said: "When it comes to the command of PJP formations, they were commanded by Obrad Stevanovic. I know that in 1997 he became assistant minister."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say any untruth here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So Obrad Stevanovic was in command.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Up to 1997, definitely and then he became minister and in the hierarchy that's a few steps above, and I don't know whether he continued to be in command of those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Zivaljevic can we please look at the following page the continuation of this paragraph command and control --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one thing you should bear in mind when dealing with these questions, Mr. Stevanovic may well come here and tell us what his position is, and that's one thing, but perhaps much more important is to know what other people's impression was of his position. So it's important that we get a full account of what your understood his position to be. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can we now turn to the second page -- or to the other page. Would you please read the first paragraph on the following page?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in English that's on the same page, and in the Serbian it moves on to the fourth page. We can keep the same page in the English.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: The paragraph starts with the following words: "When at the same area or on the same task there are several establishment units intervening, in that case command, control, and coordination shall be united and regulated by a special order, in principle by forming a Joint Command."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In this case when several units intervene in the same area, is this method of command and control and coordination -- or, rather, was it continued in 1998 and 1999, the same method?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I've explained just a bit ago that the conditions changed. These documents were passed earlier when we didn't have these anti-terrorist activities. We functioned -- or, rather, it's just the police force that functioned under these circumstances. This is the essential difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So in 1998 and 1999 the police forces worked on the basis of this principle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I said that the conditions had changed. Up until that time, up until 1998, it's just the police forces that operated there whenever there was a disruption in law and order or there was a large gathering or there was some incidents, riots, and so on, but then the conditions changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What do you mean? In what sense?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Because after this time we had anti-terrorist combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So what did that change in the command system in conducting anti-terrorist combat within the police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, within the police, the police wasn't ready for these tasks because those were just regular policemen that were supposed to ensure just basic security.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, this is -- this is setting out the procedure, albeit set out in the early 1990s rather than the late 1990s, and the simple question is: Did the paragraph that you read continue to apply as the appropriate guidance in 1998 and 1999? Now, that's different from whether and how it was implemented, but was that the rule that should have been implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only within the police force, but it wasn't just the police that wasn't involved at this point. It was also the army, and that significantly changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, it doesn't even apply to the police in general. It's more specific than that. It only applies to the special police units and that's clear when you read it. We know that. We know it's got nothing to do with the army. So please answer the questions that are being put to you. On the basis they're being put to you. Was this the way the special police were supposed to operate? Now, what's the answer to that question? Did it apply in 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In you're looking for an answer, then I can tell you this: Within my detachment where I worked, I had my parts of the unit, and all parts, I'm referring to commanders of companies and so on, they were all answerable to me in that sense. That's within my purview that I can tell you about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I specifically said to you don't deal with what happened in practice. Don't deal with the change in circumstances on the ground. Tell us whether in principle this is the rule that ought to operate in 1998 and 1999. I hope the question is now clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this rule did not change, then it was supposed to be in operation, and I don't know that the rule was changed, but the factual situation on the ground was frequently different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, who did you receive orders from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I've told you. When I came to Podujevo, in a dispatch that I received from the chief of the sector it was clearly stated what was my destination, where I was supposed to arrive, and what was my objective there and that I was supposed to stay there for a while, and a unit that was supposed to be with me was specified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm going to have to deal with this, Mr. Zivaljevic. You were asked just now a very simple question, unless there is something peculiar about the translation and no one has drawn that to my attention, and the question was: Who did you receive orders from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received the order from the chief of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the order for you to carry out an anti-terrorist action, you would receive such an order from whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I received orders pertaining to a task, and that task was a complex one and it comprised perhaps two or three actions. I acted in accordance with that task. As for orders, I would receive them in advance, and I acted in accordance with them. I had a basic order. I did not receive different orders on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. You explained to us how you received orders and maps. Did you ever have an independent anti-terrorist action without the participation of the army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I normally assisted the secretariat in the territory where I was. So, for example, if the secretariat needed five or six policemen for regular duties to arrest somebody and so on, I would give them a reinforcement, a squad to assist them. So in that sense, only purely police work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you asked a question at line 4 on page 56 of the transcript: "So the order for you to carry out an anti-terrorist action, you would receive such an order from whom?" Now, that questions has not been answered. Do you not want the answer? Because if you don't want the answer, we want it. So it would be helpful for you to pursue that and get an answer to your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I attempted to put a follow-up question. I asked him whether he received an order from assistant chief of sector for a specific action, but let me ask again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For a specific action, be it an independent one or one conducted jointly with the army of Yugoslavia, who would you receive an order from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you this: The dispatch sending me to perform a task in Podujevo and to take part in anti-terrorist activities specified that I was to go to Podujevo, to stay there, to get involved with the military group operating in that area and to act in accordance with the plan, the plan that I received from the army and to participate in those activities in accordance with that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So let me stop you here. So the assistant chief of sector ordered you in that dispatch to act in accordance with the army plans.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: To get involved in those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To work in accordance with the army plans. And you are sitting here under oath telling us you received such an order from assistant chief of sector or the minister. Was that in writing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well you're asking me I don't have that dispatch in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you that in the dispatch it was specified exactly what my destination, location stay there was all about, what transportation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bakrac is the reference to the assistant chief of the sector? I've obviously missed something.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is possible that I made a mistake. I can't follow the transcript and the answers. Let me ask again just to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who signed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the question who is issuing these instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who issued the order sending you to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: The dispatch was signed by the chief of the public security sector Vlastimir Djordjevic. Now, whether he had received his orders from the minister I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And in that order he told you what? When did you first receive that dispatch? When were you sent down there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Sometime in the second half of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: 1999. In that dispatch --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Just a second. Just answer what I'm asking you. So prior to the second half of March, you were not in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I was in Kosovo in January.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On the same?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Not on the same on a different task and I can explain that if necessary; and then I had a break I stayed in Belgrade and then I received a dispatch to go there in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To go to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And to resubordinate yourself to it the army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it in those terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What did you receive as a task and what was your order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you again I suggest that you take a look at this dispatch. This dispatch says where I was supposed to go to, to what area, with what forces, using what transportation, and what was my objective during my stay there. It was all specified there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Just a second. So it was all specified in detail including the transportation that you were going to use.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And from that moment on nothing on was specified in detail of what you were going to do from there on, on the 24th the 25th the 26th who was supposed to decide on that your participation and action and anti-terrorist activities of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Let me explain dispatches normally specify a period of time. For example, they say 30 days or 45 days but all of that is conditional. It was never a firm rule that the stay was going last for 30 days or for 40 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who is going to specify whether you're going to stay there for 30 days or 40 days since it wasn't specified in the dispatch how? Did you know how long you would stay there? Who would send you back?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: The conditions on the ground would send you back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And that's something you decide upon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Only within my scope of authority. I have a right to decide only within my scope of authority which is specified by the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what was your scope of authority when it came to decision-making?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was within what I had. So on the one hand I had a dispatch sending me to perform a task, and then on the other hand there was documents there pertaining to the actions that were supposed to be carried out on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So in March you had documentation pertaining to all the actions all the way until the end of June; right? Is that what you're trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I want to tell you that I knew about an action which was of a broader spectre, three larger actions pertaining to Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and another action that I can't remember just now. This activity was carried out by the Pristina Corps. They prepared the documentation. I read that documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you remember you read that documentation of the Pristina Corps and you remember it well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, not really well. It was eight years ago. I remember reading it. If you have it as evidence, you can put it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you then issue any orders to your subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Listen, based on that basic order or the maps, the commander -- you saw the map drafted by Gergar and the order. Most likely he made minor excerpts of the decision, and I adjusted, I adapted to what was there. I commanded only police units, no other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I told you, and I told Mr. Ivetic. Since I'm not qualified when it comes to military science, I'm quite ignorant there. I always relied on military commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. Now, let us stay there for a second. You relied on military commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I would like to go back to the question which I think has still not been answered, which is for specific anti-terrorist actions, from whom did you receive your orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was sent out with the general task. When I came to the field, I had an order map waiting for me, which meant a concretisation of what I was supposed to do. The maps said what I was supposed to do, and that was part of the text as well. At the meetings with the military commander who was in that area and with whom I established contact when I arrived, I roughly -- well, not roughly, but I found out in greater detail what it was that we were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, what is the number of the document which originally sends the witness to Kosovo? And if you don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it right this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Ivetic can give me a number for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6D291. 6D291.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, I'm asking you the following: These documents were there waiting for you. I'm asking you whether the military commander Gergar or anyone else commanded you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the first stage I cannot explain it that way, that he commanded. Please. I explained what it was that I could know and what it was that I could not know. He always explained the map, the direction, the axis and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, you were commander of a big intervention brigade, the 122nd. I'm asking you whether Gergar, Colonel Gergar, commanded you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call that command. I cooperated with Gergar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Cooperation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Please, but there were two stages involved. Do you understand me? Sometime in April, I don't know when this happened, there were documents there that - how should I put this - that pertained to subordination or resubordination actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: At any point in time were you resubordinated to the army of Yugoslavia and Colonel Gergar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, not literally but I cooperated and heard his opinions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now, you said that since you did not complete a school for commanding artillery units you were not versed in carrying out this kind of action and reading maps. How did it happen that you were appointed commander of a big PJP detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume that my superior officers could be in a better position to tell, but I will try to explain. I worked in the Belgrade SUP from 1975, so my authority, in view of these policemen from Belgrade, was at quite a high level. I had a great influence over the police, and they listened to me, and I was devoted to them in the sense of taking care of them and not exposing them to danger, and they appreciated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivaljevic, you said a few moments ago and also during the direct examination, I noted that down, that often precisely because of your lack of knowledge in anti-terrorist action conduct you asked the commanders of the army of Yugoslavia. My question is the following: Do you know that the head of the staff of the MUP in Kosovo completed the military academy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know that the assistant head of staff of the MUP in Kosovo, Mr. Mijatovic, also completed the military academy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know that Dusan Adamovic, an operative or whatever he was on the staff completed the military academy.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know that Obrad Stevanovic and you say that you saw him as commander of the PJP, that he graduated from the military academy as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are all these persons -- were all these persons within the same organ that you were in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: They all worked in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So why didn't you consult with them with regard to military matters and with regard to your lack of knowledge, et cetera? Why did you consult this military commander, a colonel at that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I'll give you a simple explanation. I saw them very seldom. Often I could not even see them, or our communications were interrupted. It was wartime. There was bombing and often communication were interrupted, so I could not establish contact with them. That is one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to go back to my previous question, Mr. Zivaljevic. Are you claiming here today to us before this court that you never carried out any independent anti-terrorist action without the participation of the army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Please, this action as an action I did not carry out, but sometimes I had some returns or exits or movement towards an area or I couldn't pass, but there is this one basic thing that I'm going to tell you right now. It had to do with the following: The police wherever they went they never used weapons until weapons were used against them. I don't know what it is that you have in mind, but I did not plan this. I don't know how to draw a map. Also, this order I don't know, but the police work I had to carry out, I did carry out, and from time to time there was some work there that required perhaps, in relation to crime or some other activity, some activity that was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you don't know how to draw a map. Do you know how to read a map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, I practised that through my work. I am not a person who is a slow learner. I managed to fit into this, but I always needed someone who would help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, a few moments ago you said that you had a military assistant or, rather, an assistant from the MUP who was a graduate of the military academy.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but often we were not together. You know, we were a unit that was separated in two different areas. The fact that this is a big unit did not really affect the part where I was, because the other part was commanded by Bosko Buha in the area of Pec. That is over 100 kilometres away from the place where I was. We had small units and then we separated them. In total these two units made up this --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Your deputy, was he a military academy graduate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did he know how to read a map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part he did when we were together but very often we were separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Zivaljevic, let us look at 5D1418. Could we please have a look at the second page of this document first, and the ERN number is 534130. The next one, please. Mr. Zivaljevic, I -- it seems that this is a telegram of the 122nd Intervention Brigade and the signature says Dragan Zivaljevic. Can you have a look at it telegram, and can you tell us whether you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I recognise the telegram. May I give a comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I am going to put questions to you. So you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who is this telegram sent to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. 122nd Intervention Brigade, civilian persons should is be returned to their village --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm not asking you to read it out. I'm asking who it was sent to this telegram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: The MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The number --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: It says to the Chief of Staff of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, sorry, sorry. I beg you pardon. I asked for the second page of the 25th. The next one, please. The third one in actual fact. The cover page would be the first page. The next page, please. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I recognise it, but there are some problems in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. You're going to explain it to us what kind of problems? First of all, who was this document sent to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: The MUP of the republic of is Serbia sent -- actually, the 122nd Intervention Brigade to the chief of staff of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. This is your signature, Dragan Zivaljevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but I have to give an explanation in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who is the chief of staff of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: It is completely the other way around. The communications person who was supposed to do this didn't even know what the name of the staff was and who headed the staff. Since the communications were broken down because of the NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I understand. Just a second, please. Please pause there. Let's do this one thing at a time. Did you sign this telegram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Not at this moment. There weren't conditions for that, and later on he brought this to me, what it was that he had sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: He sent a telegram without your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, not without my knowledge, but he did not know how to write a proper heading. You see, we had this activity of returning civilians --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please take it slowly, Mr. Zivaljevic. What was the heading of the telegram supposed to be like?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: To the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. To the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: There is no chief of staff. This is completely wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. To the MUP staff. Please be so kind as to tell us now the attained lines Bora 1. What does Bora 1 mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say that right now what Bora 1 was in this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this is a name for the map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know on maps there are these little circles that denote particular points that had been attained or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm asking you what Bora 1 is, then after that you have the points of attainment. What is Bora 1, the lines attained, Bora 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember. "The lines attained, Bora 1." I assume that it's some kind of a call-sign. It changed, let me tell you that. Sometimes once a week. It is really hard to go back to that time, remember everything and give a specific answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know on the 26th of May what does this action pertain to? This telegram, rather, pertains to what action? The date is the 26th of May.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: It pertains to a humanitarian action, the return of civilian persons to their places of residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Fine. Humanitarian action of the return of civilian persons. Tell us, what does "Grey 0" mean? Perhaps I can jog your memory.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's do it this way -- let's have a look, and then we'll go back to this document. 5D1427. The last page, please. The last page of this document. The last one, please. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection to the question, Your Honour, insofar as the document that's being referred to. There is no basis for this foundation that this relates to the same time period or to the same activities insofar as the title of the same is indeed temporary directory and relates to a different region, et cetera. So unless, unless they can -- counsel can show that this is something that relates to this witness I don't think that the question is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave. I think that the question is quite appropriate. This witness here has his own telegram right in front of him here, one that he signed. He has this wording "Grey 0," and I would like to know whether he can link this up with the list of code signs of the MUP that was operational at one point in time in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The objection's repelled. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, please look at the second row, the last column under "Grey" and "0". On the right-hand side. Is that a code for "I have some wounded persons"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: That is what it means, but could you please lower this a bit so that I can see the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Fine, we can do that, but I'm just asking you is that what it meant in your telegram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Please, my man who worked on radio communications sent this report. Now I am interpreting this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Just a second, please. He sent this report without your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Please, I sent it -- or, rather, I told him to send a report, and he tried to make do because he could not do it through regular channels. We didn't have radio communication. Perhaps he sent this through the communications map. You know -- do you understand what the situation was? All our repeaters were broken down every other day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you telling this telegram didn't receive the staff --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to give you an answer very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's just calm it down. You've been asked a question about the meaning of your telegram. Now, can you help us with the use of the expression "Grey" and "0"? Now that you've seen this, does it help you to tell us what Grey and 0 stood for in the telegram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that there is a meaning involved, but I just suggest that we have a look at the date of this document. So can I please have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there a problem about looking at the date, Mr. Bakrac? Let's lack at the date then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date is on the first page, but, Your Honour, I believe that the witness will trust me. It is Pristina 1998.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, please lift it a bit so that I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just scroll down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's see the bottom of the document. Where is -- where is the date on the document, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pristina 1998, here it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, having seen that, Mr. Zivaljevic, can you help us to interpret your telegram?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would say that it's the correct text, but I'm afraid it changed from time to time. This instruction changed from time to time. I don't know if there were any changes here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that. You've said all that. Just let's concentrate on the question I'm asking you. Having seen this, does that help you to interpret "Grey" and "0" in your telegram?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. It's okay. I believe that telegram is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You believe what in -- just tell us what these words meant or said in the telegram.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose it meant that we had one person wounded or injured according to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that what it was? I think one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. It says: "There are some wounded. I have some wounded persons."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Is there a number in brackets?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. Grey 0 means "I have some wounded."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: That's one in the telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I suppose then it's one person. Could we go back to the telegram? It would be of assistance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. I thought you were going to take us back once you'd done this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Oh, sorry. It's still not there. 5D1417 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, it's 5D1418, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I said, 1418. Next page, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, you said it was an exclusively humanitarian action. What does this mean? If we described Grey 0. What does it mean "We had several resistance points"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I have to explain one thing here. At one point we had a movement of refugees from Podujevo, and columns of people of 30.000 plus citizens, and we were looking for options how to react to persuade these people to go back to their homes and guarantee their safety. Prior to that we had talks with the municipality and with the army and tried to reach an agreement, but on the ground something unexpected happened. When we saw the refugees coming down from hills, we noticed in front of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: None of this is essential for the point that counsel to trying to make. Mr. Ivetic may want to explore it further with you in due course. We just want you to make it clear to us what this says about wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I meant to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... was there more than one wounded. That's the only question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one sentence if you allow me. In front of the refugees there was a unit of Siptar terrorists and one behind, and we could not safely approach the refugees to talk to them. We used people who knew --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, tell us whether this document refers to one wounded or more than one wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to this document I see one wounded. In brackets it says: "One not so seriously."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all the question was about. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: My next question is: What does it mean: "Positions taken up 86 and 109"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know them. I don't have the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Not on the map. Just explain to us in simple terms 87, 86, 109 positions taken up.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Those are the positions where our units are located.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: "Taken up" what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: When we get there and we take up these positions, those are positions taken up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what do these numbers mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: These are numbers on the map, markings. When you draw the mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That means the MUP staff to which you sent this dispatch has the same map as you do in order to be able to follow the numbers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Please, not infrequently --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's a simple question in order to be able to follow these numbers about positions taken up the MUP staff receiving your dispatch had to have a map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: It was through the MUP staff that we frequently received maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac 5D1427 is untranslated. Is that -- what's the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I cannot say now which is 5D1427.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... for 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can verify, Your Honour, with my assistant. I believe it was submitted for translation because it has already been used with one other witness. My colleague Mr. Cepic -- that witness, I believe it was witness Mijatovic but I'm not sure. I suppose it was submitted for translation back then, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic is challenging its authenticity or are you not, Mr. Ivetic? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I challenge its applicability to the time period based on earlier, but if I could assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's my inaccurate recollection of your challenge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can assist as I believe a review of the trial transcript will reveal, when this was used previously I intervened to advise that it has a P number, a P exhibit, and a translation. I don't have that information at hand, but I do recall the circumstances of that exhibit being tendered and I believe it was through the Witness Deretic rather than Mijatovic although it might have been used with as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It was reference to a temporary -- I'm sorry I had some notion in my head that you'd referred to as a draft, but it was temporary, which clarifies it. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour if I may what Mr. Ivetic says rings a bell. I believe it's P1071, and there is an English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's very helpful. No point in duplicating translation, Mr. Bakrac. So after today would you please check the position and if there is a translation available make sure that you don't take up time with another one and use the one that's translated in future. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, here in the telegram you stated there were around 150 fighting men. Did you mean the fighting men of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The fighting men of the KLA who followed the refugees, which means they accompanied them, moved along with them in an organised manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you requested further instructions concerning these columns of refugees, and you even requested points, I suppose encrypted points, where they settled down.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I believe so. But if I may add one thing --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. I asked you, did you request further instructions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose I asked for an opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Let's stop here. Could you please read the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: You're right. Request further instructions. And I believe I asked them to indicate locations where we could put up the refugees because they wouldn't turn back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Since Mr. Ivetic let you read some handwriting, could you try again with some handwritten comments. What's written, for instance, in the right upper corner in Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: On this document? Arsa.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me stop you. Can you help us? Who is Arsa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I believe Arsa was an officer who was helping out at the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Last name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: If that's the one I mean, it's Arsenijevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you go on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: General Lukic, for information and decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know whose signature this is. Maybe you can help me, but I can't recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does it look like the signature of the Deputy Mijatovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: There is a letter M here, but I don't know his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. There was a Colonel Mijatovic -- or, rather, Mr. Mijatovic who was here, and he explained it. I was just asking if you were familiar with his signature.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could we now turn one page back. Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: It's a reply from the staff saying they agree that the refugees go back to a safe place and they be put up -- I don't know if it was specified here where. We were in contact with the refugees, you know, and we sent out people who -- all right. All right. I won't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: "Militarily able persons to be taken into custody and turn over to the nearby secretariat."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, concerning elevations where you would put up these people and what to do with the militarily able men, you asked for the staff's decision, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: In part that would be true, because in the municipality, the decision-making process about what to do with these people was already under way, and the municipality could decide what to do with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And this is an instruction what to do with militarily able men.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: That's regular police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that for things like this you asked for approval and instructions what to do, whereas for performing combat operations with the army of Yugoslavia you acted on plans and whatever the brigade commander ordered you on the ground?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: You have to understand one thing. It was a humanitarian activity that required the involvement of a number of participants and it was a serious problem with the movement of population.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We see here that you had combat activities, one person wounded. You provided the positions taken up. You had 150 fighting men against you, and you're telling me it's not a combat activity.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: If you give me two minutes I'll explain, with your permission. We were facing a problem, how to approach these civilians. Siptar terrorists opened fire on us. We did not respond lest we hurt the civilians, but we used people who wielded some authority from the SUP Podujevo and people from that municipality, locals who knew the language. We sent them to talk to the refugees to try to persuade them to go back. We couldn't talk to them directly they didn't know us. They saw us in a completely different light, but we used these go-betweens to try to persuade them to go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were the 150 able-bodied men taken into custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. We do not reach them. They either dispersed or laid down their arms and joined the mass of people. It's very inhospitable area. I was watching all that from a distance of a height of about 400 metres. Fire was opened on us and we were not able to get anywhere near them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you help us with timing, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will use the break to try to abbreviate my cross. I hope it won't take more than another 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis, prospects of completing the witness today or none?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: They're growing dimmer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we have to break for lunch at this point, Mr. Zivaljevic. Could you again please leave the courtroom with the usher, and we will see you again at 1.45. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.46 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon again, Mr. Zivaljevic, before we went on the break we looked at the document which had a list of code signs of MUP. Did you know that the army of Yugoslavia used quite a different type of documents for conveying information which is known under the acronym TKT or secret command of troops and that it has nothing to do with the code list that we looked at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you anything about that. I don't know anything about military code lists. I never used them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. So that's what I was interested in. You did not use military list of code signs. Now, could we -- could we look at 6D709, which is the order for Palatna. Mr. Ivetic showed you that order. Could we now see page 1. Do you have a hard copy with you? All right. Then let us turn to the last page of this document. Could we now see the last page, please, page 5 in B/C/S. You saw item 13 command and signals. Would you please read this, the third paragraph commences with the words --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: "When carrying out combat operations, maintain radio and telephone communications with the Pristina Corps command on channel 48 SD reserve channel 51 SD and within the brigades and battalions maintain radio communications using the simplex channel, channel 15 for 211th Armoured Brigade and channel 17 for 354th."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivaljevic. Do you recognise any MUP units here or any channels used by MUP?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I do not recognise the units. As for channels, I can't remember. I can't be certain. I don't think these are police channels. I'm not sure about that, but I definitely do not recognise these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivaljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. We were just checking the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, please look at item 14 now. Reports to be forwarded, and then it says "Regular reports on readiness to launch attacks and daily reports by 1800 hours reporting the situation at 1700 hours." Did you have any duty to report pursuant to this order where it says reports to be forwarded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether this pertained to the military command within the brigade that was on the ground or within the Pristina Corps, but this is their document and they have their own deadlines for the reporting which did not correspond with ours. We were on the ground together, and they reported to their command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That's exactly what I wanted to ask you. You said, if I'm not mistaken, that Nikolic informed you about this action, about this situation on the ground, and that you reported further on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. This is not the same action. This is another action.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: My mistake then. So did you report further on about this particular action that I just put to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I had several people who were specially trained for the communications system within my unit, and we had our own relays which were targeted on a daily basis. I had to change seven or eight relays because they had been hit by NATO and were marked as a target, so I had problems. Very often I had no communication at all except the simplex lines within unit. For example, we had several stations within the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm interested in this: Your subordinated units report to you. Who do you report to further on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: If possible, my companies would report me during the day whenever they could. If not, we would meet in the afternoon. Usually I did not inform anyone or report to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You didn't report to anyone?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Except in some urgent situations where people needed medical assistance. They needed to be taken care of or their families needed to be notified when somebody was killed. It is then that there was a need to have somebody go across the border and then use a telephone line there or have somebody go to Pristina and then make a phone call from there, but those were difficult circumstances because it wasn't safe to move about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And who did you report to then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we would either inform the families or provide medical assistance, dependent on the situation if a person was gravely wounded, we needed to take care of that person or sometimes if somebody was killed we had to notify the family to take over the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you did not inform the military command about that either; right? You did not report to them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Military command had its own chain of reporting and we did our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you now read paragraph 14, item 14 of this same document. It seems to me that something was either mistranslated or not translated at all. Would you please read this sentence slowly.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: "Joint action between elements of combat disposition in the course of planning, organising, preparation, and carrying out of combat activities in the sector of the village of Palatna shall be organised by the command of the 211th Armoured Brigade which is in charge of planning, organising, and carrying out combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this paragraph here talks about joint action?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I do not challenge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me then since this is a military document the command of the 211th Armoured Brigade shall be in charge of planning, organising, and carrying out combat activities in relation to their own units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I had to adapt my activities to these plans. I did not have other plans. I acted in accordance with these orders and plans. I had no other plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. Now that we're dealing with these plans, could we now see P1990. And this has something to do about the topic that we covered at the beginning of our cross-examination, which is your arrival in the territory of Podujevo and three major actions. You said that when you came there you found maps and orders of the command.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is minutes of a meeting of the Pristina MUP staff held on the 17th of February, 1999. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, please look lines 5 and 6 from the bottom. It begins with the words "The plan of RJB was developed." Would you please read to the end of it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Would you please help me find it? Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It is line seven from the bottom. It begins the words "A plan -- the plan of the RJB was developed."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: RJB stands for public security sector in order to prevent and disallow the entrance of military forces of NATO into our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please read on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: "Once that is ordered, the -- the staff plan to carry out three actions of sweeping the terrain or -- from terrorists in the sectors of Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica, and for that forces consisting -- police forces consisting of 4.000 members, about 70 policemen from OPG and about 900 persons from reserve forces have been prepared."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, now that you've read this, do you still claim that you received the corps plans -- oh, no. First tell me, is Podujevo an area where you were located with your intervention brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: These actions, are these those that you spoke of when you said that the plans awaited you when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you didn't know that the staff planned to carry out these actions, and you didn't know the details about the strength and so on? You saw this for the first time here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Listen, this is the plan of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, no, no. The staff planned to carry out these three actions of sweeping the terrain from terrorists and so on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's why I'm mentioning the public security sector. The staff is answerable, is responsible to the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I understand that, but does it say here that the staff planned to carry out these actions? Would you please read it out again and tell me whether it says so.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm interpreting it. I'm interpreting the text. It says here that the staff planned to carry out actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you see this plan drafted by the staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have to object to the last question since it misstates the evidence. It misstates this exhibit, in fact, and I think that's clear from the way that if you look at line number -- there's no mention of a plan. It says plan to carry out. There's a difference there. Semantic difference but if we're going to be asking very precise questions we have to be careful that the precise questions precisely state what the documents that are presented are supposed to say and for that matter I don't believe we have any evidence that this witness was at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's are all matters for submission in due course, and if you wish to ask questions about it in re-examination, then that would be appropriate, but please continue, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, now let us turn to a different document which also represent minutes from a meeting with senior police officers in Kosovo and Metohija, dated 4th of April, 1999. This is P1989. It seems we have the wrong document. P1989, please. This is the OTP Exhibit 1989. Are you familiar with these minutes or do you know about this meeting? Did you attend it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I think I did attend it, the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you spoke at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Could I see the following pages? I think that this is the meeting that the gentleman asked me about in relation to Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could we see the following page, please. Or, rather, page 3, the following one. 260. We have the right page in English, and we have the B/C/S page as well. Dragan Zivaljevic, commander of the 22nd Detachment of PJP. That's you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Here you briefed and said that the task has been fully completed than the territory's under control. What did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Most likely the activities that I carried out in accordance with the plan. This is the 4th of April. If I could orient myself time-wise, that means that we were in that area near Podujevo, in that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivaljevic. Could we now please look at the next document. Record of the meeting held at the MUP staff, dated the 7th of May. P1996. Page 9, please. Page 9. Could you read point 2, anti-terrorist actions. Obrad Stevanovic is speaking at this point, assistant minister. Could you please read that paragraph number 2 out to us.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: You're asking me about paragraph 2; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: "Anti-terrorist actions." I don't have the text any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the B/C/S version has disappeared. Ah, yes, here it is again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you could please zoom?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it all right now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in part. Anti-terrorist actions in some areas progress slowly and with great difficulty. After the end of some of the larger scale actions such as Budakovo, Jezerce every SUP was expected to work independently on organising anti-terrorist actions in their respective areas. The plan has to be approved by the staff, and it will be carried out with manoeuvre detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does this jog your memory regarding the planning of anti-terrorist actions, how and where anti-terrorist actions were planned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I personally attended that meeting. However, I said that when we do not have a particular plan the SUPs partly did some work in the sense of --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, sir. You said certain work that was not anti-terrorist activity. That is why I asked you to read it from the very outset, anti-terrorist actions. That is this item on the agenda. So this pertains to anti-terrorist actions; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Please, can I just answer this question by giving an example? If a group of two or three or five or -- men break into an area, a built-up area, it can be anti-terrorist activity or it can be criminal activity or rather it can be terrorist activity or criminal activity. You know what I mean. I cannot draw a line of distinction exactly what terrorism is and what crime is; so when there were larger actions involved, we worked in that larger scale way, but when there were separate actions involved it was the is SUPs that were doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Before the break what you said to me was you were not involved in any kind of independent anti-terrorist actions, now you say that you did?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I said that we worked in accordance with the documents that we received. When there was no such activity we helped the SUPs or OUPs in some smaller-scale actions that had to do with resolving crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Not anti-terrorist action?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, if an armed group enters a settlement, perhaps they can engage in looting or arson, well, let me tell you, it can belong to the category of crime and the category of terrorism so I cannot distinguish between the two what kind this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. 5D1329. Could we please have that called up. While we're waiting for that, Mr. Zivaljevic this is the map that my colleague Mr. Ivetic showed you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Before we get to that document I hate to interrupt but we have a transcript issue that I want to clear up before Mr. Bakrac gets to his actual question. Page 9, line 8, I believe it says -- in the transcript it says cannot distinguish between the two what kind this is, I believe the witness says both are police work. I don't know how it came through on the English feed we can have that checked via the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, you have commented on this map when talking to Mr. Ivetic. I think that you said that you were familiar with this map, the decision for Bajgora.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I said it was familiar to me but I did not agree with some of the details marked on this map. I don't understand some things here I recognise the settlement, and I recognise the units on the right-hand side of the map but on the left-hand side it is completely unknown to me and something seems wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me, can you indicate to us where the 122nd Intervention Brigade of the PJP was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: If it can be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could the lower part please be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Okay. [Interpretation] The 122nd in the right-hand corner, this is what I'm marking now. And you can see that there are two companies of the 122nd Brigade. That is my interpretation now. Then the 211th is up there, and then the 354th is down below, and the 122nd is here in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you at these positions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me now --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Or approximately there. Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you allow for the possibility that you were not precisely in those positions; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say with reliability that I was at that particular point, but perhaps I was in the vicinity. I was probably with the commander of the 211th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me now, when we look at the middle you see the 58th LPBR and it says ODPLP.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give any comments on that. This is completely unknown to me and this map is unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That will do, Mr. Zivaljevic, as far as I'm concerned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you want an IC number for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour. I do apologise. However, I don't know what the next IC number is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC 191, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm bringing this to an end. This took a bit longer than I had promised.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivaljevic, could you please be so kind as to tell me, the members of your detachment wore what kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN ZIVALJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the period, the time period in which they took part. As far as I can remember, in the period of 1998, for the most part they wore camouflage uniforms for urban action, that is, the grey blue camouflage. Towards the end of that year when these uniforms could be issued, then green camouflage uniforms were issued. These were uniforms that were used subsequently, after that, in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you had grey camouflage as well?
